preconditions.description: The number of cities n must be between 4 and 1000.
The maximum allowed number of roads k must be between n-1 and 2n-2.
Cities a, b, c, and d must be between 1 and n.
Cities a and b must be distinct, and cities c and d must be distinct.

preconditions.expression: a != c and a != d and b != c and b != d
preconditions.description: Cities a, b, c, and d must all be distinct.

postconditions.description: If it's impossible, print '-1'. Otherwise, print two lines of paths.
The first line must contain exactly n distinct integers.
The second line must contain exactly n distinct integers.
The first integer in the first line must be a.
The last integer in the first line must be b.
The first integer in the second line must be c.
The last integer in the second line must be d.
All integers in the first line must be distinct.
All integers in the second line must be distinct.
The two paths must not share any cities except possibly the start and end cities.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '-1' or len(set((int(x), int(y)) for x, y in zip(return_value.splitlines()[0].split(), return_value.splitlines()[0].split()[1:]))) <= k
postconditions.description: The number of roads in the first path must not exceed k.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '-1' or len(set((int(x), int(y)) for x, y in zip(return_value.splitlines()[1].split(), return_value.splitlines()[1].split()[1:]))) <= k
postconditions.description: The number of roads in the second path must not exceed k.
